newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police said to hold serial killer suspect.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police said to hold serial killer suspect.

text.p: Belgian police were said on Tuesday to be holding a suspected serial killer following the weekend discovery of bin bags containing the surgically severed body parts of four women.
Belgian media reported the suspect had contacted police before attempting to kill himself. He was presently in hospital.
The investigating magistrate charged with overseeing the inquiry was not immediately available to confirm the reports.
Belgian police have so far found eleven plastic rubbish sacks containing severed limbs. In one sack there was a torso.
"It is the torso of a woman aged between 35 and 40 years," a spokesman for the public prosecution service said on Monday. "It looks like it is a fourth victim...and it is quite recent."
"It could be the work a serial killer," he said in reply to a question.

Bags containing the arms and legs of the three other victims were found by chance by a mounted policeman in a ditch next to the Brussels-Paris railway line on Saturday in the town of Cuesmes near Mons in southern Belgium.
The torso was discovered on Monday.
All the remains have been transferred to Liege University hospital where forensic pathologists have the task of piecing together the anatomical jigsaw.
Mons Public Prosecutor Pierre Honore warned that identification of the victims could take some time.
"It will be slow. At least 15 days," he told RTBF television.
Police said it was clear from the state of the ground under the bags containing the severed limbs that they had been left in the ditch at different times.
Police officials said at the weekend there was no immediate reason to suspect a link with gruesome discoveries made in a paedophile scandal which has rocked the country in the past nine months.
